facts.text: SuperCam Laser Marks was deployed at Jezero Crater during Perseverance (Mars 2020) in 2021.

SuperCam fires a laser at rocks from up to 7 metres away, vaporising a tiny spot and analysing the flash of light to determine chemical composition. It can also use Raman spectroscopy to identify minerals and organic compounds. The small pits left by the laser on Martian rocks are among the most precise human-made marks on another world.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Analyses rock chemistry from up to 7 metres away using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy, detecting minerals and organic compounds remotely.
SuperCam's laser pits on Martian rocks are among the most precise human-made marks on another world; its data guides which rocks Perseverance drills.
